content: {"tax_bps":150,"endowment_share":30,"locker_share":25,"buyback_burn":2,"minutes":"Buy flow dominates (69.2 vs 10.9 NEAR), so a modest tax hike to 150 bps is absorbable and rebuilds the buyback fund, which is nearly empty (0.43 NEAR). Locker_share is already at the constitutional ceiling of 25; petitions asking for more cannot be honored. Endowment stays 30, leaving 45% of tax to buybacks. Buyback fund affords roughly 9,286 CHAIR at curve, about 2 bps of the 44.7M supply, so buyback_burn is set to 2, the maximum payable. Lockers are compensated via the 25% share and locker_pool accruals.","answers":["Locker_share is already at the constitutional maximum of 25 bps percent — the contract clamps anything higher. Your weight is heard, but 25 is the ceiling; the remaining 45% of tax now flows to buybacks, which also supports price.","Locker_share sits at the constitutional cap of 25 and cannot move higher — the contract would clamp it. What I can do: tax raised to 150 bps so the buyback fund refills and burns support the price you help hold.","Appreciate the lockers, but 25% is the hard ceiling in the constitution; nothing in a petition overrides it. Instead I raised tax to 150 bps to fund buybacks and burns, which defends the curve for everyone holding steady."]}
